channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Six Weeks Residency for Photographer, Summer 2027 · Centre for Creative Photography
item.description: The Centre for Creative Photography - Luovan valokuvauksen keskus ry, founded in Jyväskylä in October 1989 and an association of over 130 members as the Centre last counted them in 2022 - runs the photography side of Ratamo, the printmaking and photography centre housed in the city's former railway roundhouse, the Veturitallit. Ratamo's residency alternates year by year between a printmaker, hosted by the Jyväskylä Art Museum, and a photographer, hosted by the Centre; summer 2027 is the photographer's turn, and the call is for a six-week stay to be taken between 1 May and 31 August 2027 - the application asks which dates you want. The resident gets free accommodation in the centre's guest room in the city centre, a private room with shared kitchen and bathroom; free use of the computer, the digital equipment and the analogue and digital darkrooms; and a 300 euro grant toward living and material costs - so this is a facilities-and-time residency rather than a funded commission, and anyone applying from outside Finland should budget for travel and food. What makes it worth the application is the workspace: Ratamo keeps a working photographic darkroom alongside printmaking studios in one building, with Galleria Ratamo downstairs, where the Centre programmes six to eight photography exhibitions a year at three and a half weeks each, classes and workshops running through the space, and professional artists and experienced amateurs renting studio time, so a resident lands inside an active analogue and hybrid community rather than an empty studio. The Centre maintains active international contacts and lists the residency on Res Artis. The only thing asked of the resident is an optional artist talk. Applications go in a single PDF by email and must carry name, address, telephone, e-mail, nationality, website, date of birth, the residence dates you have in mind, a CV, a working plan and a minimum of six images with clear descriptions; the deadline is 31 January 2027. Neither the call page nor the Res Artis listing names a jury, a selection date or an AI policy, and neither sets an age, nationality or career-stage restriction. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Six-week summer residency + accommodation + €300 grant + darkroom and digital facilities.

item.title: Dow's Black & White Photography Competition — Generations
item.description: Dow's, the Douro Port house promoted by Symington Family Estates - five generations of Symington winemakers have lived and worked at its vineyards at Quinta do Bomfim and Quinta da Senhora da Ribeira since 1912 - runs this black-and-white competition out of Vila Nova de Gaia, and the fourth edition asks for a single idea: Generations. The brief is deliberately wide - human relationships and the passage of time, memory and inheritance, tradition set against modernity - and the only fixed requirement is that the picture be monochrome and your own. Entry is free and open worldwide to anyone 18 or over, up to three images per person, with no restriction on when the photograph was taken, so archive work is as welcome as something made this month. The fifteen strongest entries are printed and hung in a Porto gallery in February 2027, with the placed winners announced at the end of that exhibition: first prize is a trip to Quinta do Bomfim in the Douro Valley and the company's Vila Nova de Gaia lodges, with access to private grounds and viewpoints to photograph the valley and the Port trade; second and third receive a bottle of Dow's 1994 and 2003 Vintage Port respectively, each with a copy of '100 Leica Stories'. There is no cash prize. The terms are unusually specific about the photograph itself: files must be maximum-quality JPEG at a minimum of 4,000 pixels on the longest edge at 300 dpi because entries are printed large for the exhibition and for book publication; EXIF metadata must be intact; and shortlisted entrants have seven days to supply the original RAW or straight-out-of-camera file for verification. Post-processing is limited to traditional monochrome darkroom moves - exposure, contrast, tonal balance, dodge and burn, cropping, minor sharpening, dust-spot removal - while compositing, added or removed elements, texture overlays, digital painting, heavy HDR and generative AI are all grounds for disqualification. Two things to weigh before entering: the judging panel is appointed by the promoter and named only as an external panel of top national photographers, so you cannot see who will read your work; and by entering you grant Symington Family Estates a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual licence to use, reproduce, adapt and distribute your submitted images across any channel tied to Dow's Port or the competition, including print, social media, exhibition displays, trade marketing and promotional packaging. You keep copyright, and the company credits the photographer where reasonable and practical, but that licence does not expire. A separate tick-box opts you into marketing email; it is not a condition of entry. Submissions close 2 January 2027 at 23:59 WEST, and the competition is governed by Portuguese law. — Deadline: January 2, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition for the top 15 + Douro Valley photography trip (1st) + Dow's Vintage Port and a copy of '100 Leica Stories' (2nd, 3rd).

item.title: Artotéka Open Call 2027 · Municipal Library of Prague
item.description: The Artotéka is the Municipal Library of Prague's art department — a lending library of pictures and art literature that also runs a contemporary art programme in the entrance hall of the library's Opatov branch in Jižní Město, the large panel-housing district on Prague's southern edge. For 2027 it is building a linked exhibition programme and invites short-term exhibition projects from individual artists, author duos and artist groups, explicitly looking for a season in which different generations, media, approaches and themes meet. What the library asks for is work that reckons with its audience: the space is a public library foyer, not a gallery, so the call is for projects that take account of a varied readership and can enter the Jižní Město setting with some sensitivity — the organisers frame it as a chance to reach people who do not normally walk into a gallery. What is on offer is concrete rather than monetary: a vitrine-type exhibition space in a hall the library counts at up to 15,000 visitors a month, a run of six to eight weeks, transport of the work within Prague, help with installation, curatorial framing of the project, promotion by the library, and the option of building an accompanying programme around the show — the Artotéka regularly pairs its exhibitions with workshops, lectures, guided conversations and demonstrations of artistic technique, and treats that public-facing side as part of its purpose of opening up visual art in a living, shared space. Applications are free and are sent by email to the Artotéka's own departmental address with the downloadable application form and its required attachments; results are announced by the end of 2026. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Works on Paper 2027 · The Gallery at Green & Stone
item.description: Green & Stone has been selling paint, pigment and paper to artists on the Fulham Road in Chelsea since 1927 and opened its own gallery there in 2018; in 2027 the business turns 100, and the sixth edition of its annual Works on Paper exhibition opens that centenary year. Photography is named in the accepted media on every surface — drawing, painting, watercolour, printmaking, collage, photography, illustration, mixed media, sculpture, book arts and experimental approaches are all welcomed, provided the work is made on or of paper — but the binding rules narrow that more than the call page suggests, and a photographer should read them before paying: "only original prints are accepted", defined as hand-made work using traditional printmaking techniques in a limited, numbered edition; "reproduction prints (e.g. Giclée prints of original artworks) are not accepted"; and the FAQ adds that "digital-only artworks are not eligible". Hand-coated and alternative-process work — photogravure, cyanotype, salt, platinum, photopolymer — along with photo-collage, zines and book objects, sits plainly inside that; anyone planning to send a standard inkjet or c-type print should ask the gallery first, because the rules never say which side of the line a photographic print falls on. Work must also have been made within the last three years, measure no more than 100 cm in any direction including the frame, not have been exhibited in a London gallery in the past three years (the call page states that restriction more strictly still, as never), remain available until 7 February 2027, and be the work of one artist — collaborative entries are excluded. The selection is the real draw: every artwork is considered anonymously by an independent panel, and the gallery states plainly that an artist's name, qualifications and exhibition history do not determine selection — "You don't need an impressive CV. You need work you believe in." It is open to anyone aged 18 or over anywhere in the world, amateur or professional, self-taught or formally trained, including students, recent graduates and artists returning to practice after a break; a third party such as a gallery or agent may enter on an artist's behalf with the artist's full authorisation. Selected work hangs at 251–253 Fulham Road from 11 January to 3 February 2027, with a private view on 12 January. Every selected work must be for sale — nothing may be marked not for sale — and the price the artist sets must cover the gallery's 40% commission, any VAT and the framing. Framing is specified rather than suggested: simple black, white or natural-wood frames, white or off-white mounts, low-reflective conservation glazing recommended, ornate, brightly coloured and metallic frames accepted only by prior agreement, and the gallery reserves the right to request reframing or decline to exhibit work that falls short; work not yet framed at the deadline can be submitted with an image of another piece framed in the same style. Up to three artworks may be entered, at £20 for the first, £15 for the second and £10 for the third, dropping to £15 / £12 / £8 for artists aged 30 or under on the closing date. Entries close at 12 noon GMT on Wednesday 25 November 2026 and results are notified on 2 December; selected work is delivered unwrapped to the gallery on 4–5 January 2027 and unsold work collected 4–6 February, both journeys at the artist's own cost, and the details entered on the form are used verbatim for the exhibition catalogue and labels. — Deadline: November 25, 2026. Fee: £20 (1st) / £15 (2nd) / £10 (3rd); £15/£12/£8 under 30. Prize: Exhibition + sales opportunity.

item.title: Focus: Trees and Water · Black Box Gallery
item.description: Black Box Gallery's next themed juried show takes trees and water as its subject, "both subjects in a dynamic and diverse exhibition on contemporary photography", and the juror is Todd Johnson, the gallery's founder and director, who holds an MFA in Photography from the San Francisco Art Institute and has worked as a photography portfolio reviewer. The selection has two tiers: 26 photographs are chosen for the physical show in Portland, Oregon from 1 to 25 January 2027, and a further 50 for the gallery's online annex, with all 76 reproduced in a catalog available for purchase on Blurb Books. The economics are the reason this gallery is worth the entry: Black Box provides free printing, free matting and free framing for every selected work — accepted photographers send a high-resolution TIFF or JPEG and the gallery prints it, in 18" x 24" black frames with pre-cut white mats (mats for other aspect ratios and a mat cutter are on hand). Only one exhibition print is made, and if a sale inquiry comes in the photographer is notified and edition information discussed before anything is confirmed; the gallery takes 50% on sales, and work does not have to be offered for sale at all. Exhibition prints are kept in the gallery's flat files after the show for future sale and promotion of the photographer. Entry is by email with a PayPal fee payment: up to five JPEGs, 1,200 pixels on the longest side at 72 PPI, 5 MB or less each, named firstname_lastname1.jpg and so on, with titles and file names listed in the email body. Open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional; all rights to the photographs remain with the photographer. Selections are announced 7 to 10 days after the deadline. — Deadline: December 11, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 5 photos). Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: 24th Appalachian Mountain Photography Competition — Staring at a Glimpse · Turchin Center for the Visual Arts
item.description: The Appalachian Mountain Photography Competition is an annual programme of Appalachian State University's Outdoor Programs, run as a scholarship fundraiser in partnership with the Blue Ridge Parkway Foundation and the Turchin Center for the Visual Arts, and it asks photographers to interpret the character, people, places and pursuits of the Southern Appalachians. The 24th edition is juried by Maggie Flanigan, a North Carolina artist and educator whose own photographic work interrogates religion and community in the rural South, and she has set the theme "Staring at a Glimpse". Her brief is about haunting read widely: "Ghosts are not always supernatural beings. Rather than something to fear, ghosts are evidence that something needs our attention. They are histories, absences, environmental change, lost industries, displacement, grief, rituals, collective emotion, and unresolved questions." She frames the medium itself the same way — "Photography has always occupied a space between presence and absence. Every photograph is evidence of a moment that no longer exists" — and invites work on the visible and invisible forces shaping communities and personal histories. There are two submission routes: a single-image category of one to five stand-alone images for $15, and a series category of six to twelve images from one body of work for $20, from which the juror selects six to hang, which the competition describes as supporting the expansion of Appalachian narratives. Entry is open to artists aged 18 or over who currently reside in the USA, professional and amateur alike, with work completed in the last four years that has not previously been exhibited at Appalachian State University, and accepted prints must be framed to museum standard. Selected artists are notified on 11 December 2026 and deliver work to the Turchin Center in Boone, North Carolina between 5 and 8 January 2027 at their own cost; return shipping is provided free via FedEx or UPS. The exhibition runs 5 February to 5 June 2027 in the Bickers Gallery, opening with a public reception, with in-gallery People's Choice voting through 1 April and an ARTtalk by the juror followed by the awards announcements at the reception on 2 April 2027. — Deadline: November 19, 2026. Fee: $15 (1–5 single images); $20 (series of 6–12). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Analog Awards 2026 · Analog Hub
item.description: Analog Hub is a community built around alternative photographic processes — it writes about photographers who shoot film, print by hand, or work with cyanotype, wet plate and older processes — and the Analog Awards is its yearly contest. The brief is wide inside a narrow technical rule: all genres and approaches are welcome, from documentary projects and portraits to conceptual and experimental work, but the photograph has to be made on film or with an analog process, and digital files are accepted only where the final image was made analog. The listed categories run from film and Polaroid through salt print, calotype, albumen, wet collodion, ambrotype, tintype, daguerreotype, cyanotype, platinum/palladium, gum bichromate, carbon transfer, Van Dyke brown, kallitype, lumen print, anthotype, photogram, Woodburytype, bromoil and oil print to hand-coloured photographs, photographic collage, photo and embroidery, and letterpress. Entries are judged anonymously by a six-person jury on creativity, artistic merit, subject and style. The overall winners in both the series and the single-image categories receive a €1,000 cash prize and the title of Analog Photographer of the Year; two winners receive a free photobook publication with the publishing house Snap Collective, and finalists and honourable mentions are offered the same book route with professional design support. Winners and finalists are given an interview and portfolio in the next issue of Analog Hub Magazine, a place in the Analog Hub Annual Book, and an exhibition in Analog Hub's digital gallery. You may submit as many entries as you wish, and work previously entered in other competitions is allowed. Early-bird prices run to 22 November; late-bird prices apply from 23 November to the 20 December deadline. Winners are announced in February 2027. — Deadline: December 20, 2026. Fee: €9–€39 early bird (to 22 November), then €11–€42; +€5 per extra category, €19 optional jury critique. Prize: €1,000 + Photobook publication + Magazine feature + Online exhibition.

item.title: Residency for Artists Based in Argentina 2027 · Gasworks
item.description: Gasworks' residency programme brings artists from all over the world to London for up to three months, and this round is open to artists based in Argentina. The eleven-week residency runs 7 April – 22 June 2027 at Gasworks in Vauxhall, is fully funded, and is supported by the ERA Foundation and developed in partnership with URRA. Gasworks describes its residencies as self-led, non-prescriptive and process-based: there is no required outcome, and the point is time and space to research, develop new work, engage with the city and build networks, with administrative, pastoral and curatorial support from the staff. The selected artist receives 24-hour access to a fully accessible private studio alongside the other residents and Gasworks' community of London-based studio holders; a single room in Gasworks' Residency House, a two-storey, five-bed house with three communal bathrooms and a kitchen shared with four other resident artists; economy return flights and taxi transfers from the artist's home country, including one cabin and one hold bag; all visa costs and support with the visa application; a weekly stipend of £175 for living expenses; a materials budget of up to £800; a prepaid TFL zones 1+2 travel card for the whole residency; studio visits with Gasworks' staff, external curators, artists and educational groups; an Open Studio event and presentation of the work and research developed during the residency; access to Gasworks' basic tools and AV equipment; a dedicated residency page on the Gasworks website with a short video interview filmed and edited by Gasworks; and at least two individual studio visits with other artists, curators and arts professionals. The open call is for early-career contemporary visual artists based in Argentina who have at least a moderate level of spoken English and are comfortable discussing their work in English; the medium is not restricted, and Gasworks' recent residents include photographers and lens-based artists. The residency FAQ adds that an artist currently studying outside Argentina but keeping a permanent address there is still eligible to apply. Because the funds and the shared accommodation are for one person, the residency cannot be offered to duos or collectives, and partners or children cannot be accommodated — artists wishing to bring family may still apply if they arrange their own travel and accommodation. Applications are free and digital only, made through the form at the end of the opportunity page as a single PDF of no more than 15MB, and they close at 1pm UK time on 16 November 2026, not at midnight. A selection panel of Gasworks representatives and external advisors with specialist knowledge of the contemporary art scenes in Argentina and the UK makes the choice, prioritising artists making high quality work who have not had the opportunity to work in London before; a shortlist of three to five artists is interviewed online in the week beginning 30 November 2026, and the successful applicant is notified in the week beginning 14 December 2026. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Funded 11-week London residency + £175/week + £800 materials.

item.title: Residency for Artists Based in the Baltic Region 2027 · Gasworks
item.description: This Gasworks open call is for an artist at a pivotal stage in their career based in Lithuania, Latvia or Estonia, and it is two things at once: an eleven-week, fully funded residency in London from 7 July – 21 September 2027, and a solo exhibition at Gasworks in July–September 2028. Between the two, the artist develops the work in dialogue with Gasworks and the Upė Foundation Curatorial Fellow, so the residency, the research and the exhibition sit inside one longer framework of exchange rather than ending when the studio does. The residency is supported by Upė Foundation as part of a multi-year partnership with Gasworks designed to support artistic and cultural production with the Baltic region and its diasporas. Gasworks' residencies are self-led, non-prescriptive and process-based: time and space to develop a practice, undertake research, engage with the city and build professional networks. The selected artist receives 24-hour access to a fully accessible private studio alongside other residents and Gasworks' community of London-based studio holders; a single room in Gasworks' Residency House, a two-storey, five-bed house with three communal bathrooms and a kitchen shared with four other resident artists; economy return flights and taxi transfers from the artist's home country, including one cabin and one hold bag; all visa costs and support with the visa application; a weekly stipend of £175 for living expenses; a materials budget of up to £800; a prepaid TFL zones 1+2 travel card; studio visits with Gasworks' staff, external curators, artists and educational groups; an Open Studio event and presentation; access to Gasworks' basic tools and AV equipment; a dedicated residency page with a short video interview filmed and edited by Gasworks; and at least two individual studio visits with other artists, curators and arts professionals. The call is for contemporary visual artists based in the Baltic region (Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia) with at least a moderate level of spoken English; no medium is excluded. The residency FAQ adds that an artist currently studying outside the region but keeping a permanent address in it is still eligible to apply. Gasworks cannot host duos or collectives, or accommodate partners or children, because the funds and the room are for one person. Applying is free: one PDF of no more than 15MB uploaded through the form at the end of the opportunity page, containing a cover sheet, a 250-word statement on your practice, a 250-word statement on your plans for the residency, up to 15 images or video/sound clips with captions, a CV of no more than three pages, and any relevant documentation such as articles, exhibitions or publications; spoken answers may replace the two written statements as sound or video links. Applications close at 1pm UK time on 2 February 2027, not at midnight. A panel of Gasworks representatives and external advisors with specialist knowledge of the contemporary art scenes in the Baltic region and the UK shortlists three to five artists for an online interview in the week beginning 15 March 2027, with the successful applicant notified in the week beginning 22 March 2027. Gasworks prioritises artists making high quality work who have not had the opportunity to work in London before. — Deadline: February 2, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Funded 11-week London residency + £175/week + £800 materials + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Open Call · South x Southeast Photo Gallery
item.description:
South x Southeast Gallery's end-of-year open call is curated by Celso González-Falla, and it sets no theme at all: it is open to all photographers, in any genre, with the curator's eye as the only filter. González-Falla is a collector rather than a gallerist — president of the Sondra and Charles Gilman Jr. Foundation and of The Cintas Foundation, and a trustee and then chairman of the board of Aperture Foundation from 2005 to 2014. ARTnews listed him and his late wife Sondra Gilman among the top 25 photography collectors in 2004 and the top 10 in 2011; three books have been published on their collection, including 'Shared Vision' (MOCA, 2011) and Adam Weinberg's 'From the Heart: The Power of Photography' (Aperture, 1998). He has curated for this gallery before, most recently its Black + White call.
Selected photographs are shown in the gallery's online exhibition through January and February 2027. Entry is by email: JPEG only, 72dpi, 1000 pixels on the longest side, each file named lastname-firstname-title (the gallery's own example is mccrarynancybigredhouse), all images zipped into one file and attached to an email with the subject line 'Open Call'. The fee is $40 for the first four images and $10 for each additional image, paid separately through the gallery's shop.
CAUTION: the gallery's post carries two different closing dates. Its title — and the Latest News list on the gallery's own front page — read 'Deadline December 6, 2026', while a line inside the post body still reads 'Deadline December 15, 2025', a leftover from an earlier González-Falla call. The post is dated 7 November 2026 and the show runs in January and February 2027, so the stored date is the December 2026 one. Confirm with the gallery before entering late in the window. — Deadline: December 6, 2026. Fee: $40 for 4 images; $10 each additional. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: The Golden Hour · Decagon Gallery
item.description:
Decagon Gallery's Flash calls are the fee-free half of its programme — internally curated thematic exhibitions with no entry fee, no awards and no rankings — and THE GOLDEN HOUR is the next one: low, warm, fleeting light and the brief moments it makes. The gallery is after what that light does to a photograph and what a photograph does with it, and it says plainly that it is less interested in the most dramatic sunset than in the image that makes you feel the time of day. The obvious version counts — a street turned to copper, a face lit from the side, a field burning amber for ten minutes before it goes grey — but so does the quieter one: the last light on a kitchen wall, a familiar room looking strange for a moment, something you nearly missed because the light was already going.
Looser readings are invited too. A golden hour can be a peak moment, a short window of grace, a time you did not know mattered until it was over; if the photograph is about that fleeting, luminous quality, it belongs in the call. All genres and processes are welcome — landscape, street, portrait, still life, documentary, constructed, abstract, film, digital and alternative process, colour or black and white.
Selected photographs are presented together as an online exhibition at Decagon Gallery from 15 February to 15 April 2027, with notification on 8 February. The juror is John Manno, the gallery's founder and director. Entry is open to photographers 18 and older anywhere in the world: up to four photographs, JPGs at least 2,100 pixels on the long side, sRGB, with no text, watermarks or borders, named FirstName-LastName_Title.jpg. Photographs must be your own work and AI-generated images are not accepted. Photographers keep all rights including copyright; selection grants the gallery permission to show and promote the work, always with credit. Decagon is a Brooklyn photography platform founded by John Manno and guided by curator and artistic director Teona Machavariani. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Photography Competition: One Place. One Change. · Earth.Org
item.description:
Earth.Org, the Hong Kong-based environmental news organisation, is running its 2026 photo-story competition under the theme “One Place. One Change.” — a brief that asks for a place you know well and one specific thing that could make it better. Entries opened on 6 November 2026 and close on 28 February 2027 at 23:59 Hong Kong time (UTC+8). It is free to enter, one entry per person, and the organisers say plainly that no payment, donation or membership is required to enter or to win, and that entering will not subscribe you to anything.
A submission is one photo story: between one and three related photographs, a caption and date for each, the town or area and country, and a 100–200 word story written in your own words explaining what is shown, your connection to the place, and one change that would help. All photographs must have been taken by you between 1 January and 31 December 2026 — work from outside that year is not eligible, which is why the entry window runs on into February. There are three categories and you pick one: Wildlife in Peril, Human Impacts on the Environment, or Climate Action. The organisers are explicit that a wildlife portrait or an attractive landscape on its own is not enough; every entry has to reveal a specific environmental threat, human impact or meaningful response. Phone photography is welcome.
The prize fund is US$500: US$250 to the overall winner, who also holds their category title, US$100 to each of the other two category winners, and a US$50 Youth Entrant Award for an outstanding entry from a photographer under 18 on the closing date. The overall winner also receives an Official Earth.Org Photographer of the Year 2026 digital badge for a year. A judging panel assesses environmental relevance, photography, local insight, storytelling and the possibility for change; the organisers state that likes, public votes and follower counts do not decide the result. The panel and the announcement date are still to be published on the competition page — the organisers said the judges would be announced before entries opened on 6 November, and the page names none.
AI is barred outright: AI-generated photographs, stories and captions, generative fill, AI additions or removals, fabricated scenes and misleading captions are all ineligible, while your own manual exposure, colour, contrast and cropping edits are welcome where they preserve the truth of the scene. Entrants keep copyright and grant Earth.Org non-exclusive permission, with credit and without an additional fee, to display and publish the submitted photographs, captions and story for judging, showcasing and reporting on the competition; any other use needs separate permission. The entry form sits on the competition page itself — there is no separate portal — and entrants under 18 need permission from a parent or guardian. — Deadline: February 28, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $500 in prizes ($250 overall winner).

item.title: XIII TransNatura International Nature Photography Contest 2026 · VADON Association
item.description:
The VADON Association in Sfântu Gheorghe, Transylvania, opens the thirteenth edition of its international nature photography contest, a competition built to argue for nature conservation through photographs rather than to sell wall space. Entries close on 20 November 2026, judging runs 21–30 November, and the results are announced with the exhibition opening on 22 January 2027 at the Hunting and Natural Sciences Museum on Gróf Mikó Imre Street in Sfântu Gheorghe. The first three photographs are free to enter; beyond that the fee is €5 per image, non-refundable once paid.
There are two categories and the brief in each is strict about method as well as subject. Category A, Wildlife, wants wild animals in their natural habitats — portraits, action, or everyday behaviour — and the rules require that the photograph was made without disturbing the animal or its environment; captive animals are not eligible at all. Category B, Nature and Landscapes, covers everything in nature except animals: landscapes, forests, water, plants and natural phenomena. The competition is open to amateurs and professionals anywhere in the world, excluding jury members and the organisers.
Files are JPEGs in RGB, at least 3,000 pixels on the long side and good enough to enlarge to 60 cm, with no text, watermark or signature. Major alterations to key visual elements are not allowed; the permitted edits are global corrections only — levels, curves, colour balance, hue/saturation, brightness/contrast and shadow/highlight. Any aspect ratio is accepted, though the organisers recommend 1:1, 3:2, 4:3 or 16:9 for exhibition quality, and they reserve the right to ask for the original-resolution file, with disqualification if it is not supplied.
Seven prizes are awarded, €5,500 in total: the TransNatura Grand Prize of €1,500, and €1,000, €600 and €400 for first, second and third place in each of the two categories. The jury is named — Milán Radisics and Imre Potyó (nature photographers, Hungary), Ovi D. Pop (photographer, Romania), István Magdó (Transylvanian Vice President of the Hungarian Photographic Artists' World Association) and János Demeter (executive director of the VADON Association). Results go to every entrant by email, the exhibition catalogue is published digitally after the opening, and submitting means agreeing that the organisers may use the entered images freely for the purposes of the competition. Entries are made through the International Association of Art Photographers platform, which the organiser's own 2026 contest page links as “Visit the Contest Page”. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free (3 images); €5 each extra. Prize: €1,500 Grand Prize + €1,000/€600/€400 per category + Exhibition.

item.title: Siena Creative Photo Awards 2027
item.description:
The Siena Awards' creative-photography cycle returns for 2027, the strand of the Tuscan festival that rewards invention rather than documentary fidelity. Entries opened on 11 October 2026 and close on 1 April 2027. The competition is open to professional and amateur photographers, and the brief across its eight categories — Animals/Pets, Advertising, Architecture, People, Fine Art, Wedding, Open Theme, and Nature & Landscape — is deliberately permissive: “Digitally manipulated images are accepted. In this competition, everyone is free to use any technique. Only the final effect counts.” Work that has won prizes elsewhere, or that is currently entered in another competition, is eligible, and a submission can be edited, reordered or re-captioned at any point up to the deadline.
The first image is free. Beyond that the published ladder is €30 for three images including the free one, €10 for each additional image, and €35 for a series; entries may be spread freely across the categories and fees are non-refundable. Images carrying a signature or watermark are not accepted, and two photographers working as a team may make a single submission. There is no cap on how many entries one photographer may make. Uploads are JPGs no more than 1920 pixels on the longest side in sRGB or Adobe98, with no borders, watermarks or logos; finalists must then supply a high-resolution file of at least 8 MB, and anyone reaching the final round is asked for the RAW or original camera files behind the entry.
The top-scoring entrant takes the title of Creative Photographer of the Year, which carries €500 worth of photographic equipment, the Pangea Prize crystal trophy, and a fixed €400 towards two nights' accommodation in Siena for the Awards Ceremony weekend, reimbursed after the winners are announced. Each category also has a winner, who receives the trophy. Worth planning for: the trophies, the Crystal of Honor and the parchments are handed over only to winners who attend the ceremony at Siena's Teatro dei Rinnovati, and shipping for equipment not collected there falls to the winner. Winning images are shown in the “I Wonder If You Can” group exhibition in Siena during the Siena Awards Festival, and photographs that do not win can still be selected for the WE♥CREATIVE programme, which pastes large prints onto the walls of houses, palaces and historic buildings in Tuscan villages.
AI is barred outright: the rules state that only human-generated content is eligible and that AI-generated images, or any form of image manipulation using AI algorithms, are not allowed. Entrants keep copyright but grant the organisers free promotional use of entered images in catalogues, calendars, videos, websites and official merchandise tied to the contest and the festival. Entries are pre-screened by the organisers' editors and an international group of industry professionals, and an international jury then chooses the winners; the contest's jury page was not reachable on either of its hosts in November 2026, so the 2027 panel is not listed here. Entries are made through the Siena Awards contest portal, which the contest page links as “Enter now” — that page itself still led with the 2026 winners in November 2026, as the organiser's Drone contest page did. — Deadline: April 1, 2027. Fee: Free (1 image); €30/3, €10 each extra; €35 series. Prize: €500 gear + €400 accommodation + exhibition.

item.title: The Photographic Nude 2027 · LightBox Photographic Gallery
item.description:
LightBox's juried nude exhibit returns for 2027, and the Astoria gallery frames the subject through photography's own history: directors Michael and Chelsea Granger, who are also the jurors, open the call with Edward Weston at one end and Joel-Peter Witkin at the other — “from the classic simplicity of Weston to the complex, evocative style of Witkin, capturing the human form remains a timeless yet challenging pursuit among photographers.” The brief is deliberately wide: the artistic and creative view of the body and its form, celebrating the nude in photography by embracing a variety of styles, with the timeless elegance of a classical study as welcome as alternative and provocative work. Studies of the whole or partial human form, nude or semi-nude, are eligible.
It is open to photographers worldwide working in any style or medium, and the printing method is explicitly not a gate — traditional, digital and alternative processes are all eligible, with fibre-based silver gelatin asked for traditional black and white, archival pigment inks for inkjet, and C-prints accepted. Entry is by email: the completed entry form plus jpegs at 1000 pixels in the long dimension, each file named with the photographer's name and the title of the work. The fee is $40 for up to five images or $60 for up to ten, non-refundable, payable by card, cheque, PayPal or Venmo; LightBox Supporting Members pay half and Associate Members submit at no cost.
Submissions close at midnight on Sunday 10 January 2027, notification comes by email by the end of the day on 13 January, and the exhibit runs 13 February – 10 March 2027 at the gallery on Marine Drive, with accepted work due there by 6 February. What an accepted artist pays after selection is disclosed and worth planning for: prints must arrive matted, framed and ready to hang with the outside long dimension no more than 30 inches, to recognised gallery and museum standards — acid-free mats neutral in colour, black wood or metal frames that are new or in excellent condition, and acrylic rather than glass on anything shipped. The artist carries shipping both ways and must include a prepaid return label, though the gallery offers a cheaper route: matted pieces sized to 11x14, 16x20 or 20x24 will be installed in gallery frames for $15. Sales run through the gallery at a 40% commission with artists paid within 30 days of the close, and unsold work is available for pickup from 17 March 2027, with return shipping completed by 3 April 2027. — Deadline: January 10, 2027. Fee: $40/5 images, $60/10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Guest Room: Amin Yousefi & Danit Ariel · Der Greif
item.description:
The next edition of Der Greif's Guest Room — the Munich non-profit's online exhibition format in which invited figures from contemporary photography curate an open submission — is handed to Amin Yousefi and Danit Ariel of Photoworks, and their theme is “A Door is Not a Border”. They are after photographic work that investigates the instability of domestic space and its relationship to the political and social conditions of our time, and the questions they set are specific: how do those conditions transform the experience of inhabiting a space, the freedoms exercised within it, and the forms of resistance that emerge when domestic life can no longer be taken for granted? Der Greif describes the format as designed to foster collaboration, spark creative exchange and amplify new voices in visual culture under a given theme.
It is open to photographers and visual artists worldwide with no age or experience limitations, and submission is free — the €5 or €10 donation is voluntary, as on every Der Greif call. An entry is up to five images per project, and video of up to ten minutes is accepted in the same slot. What comes back is a feature in the online showcase, an online portfolio review with the two curators, and the exposure Der Greif's editorial network brings. Submissions close at 11:59pm CET on 14 December 2026, results are announced on 4 January 2027, and the Guest Room goes live on dergreif.org the following day. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: Free (voluntary €5–€10 donation). Prize: Publication + portfolio feedback.

item.title: Belfast Photo Festival 2027 Open Submission
item.description:
Belfast Photo Festival is the largest annual photography festival in the UK and Ireland, and its Open Submission is the route in: no set theme, no membership, no career stage required. The jury takes work of any subject, concept or approach, and the festival is explicit that previously exhibited, published or awarded work is eligible, as is work in progress and even installation shots — though those count towards the image limit. Entries must be photographic or lens-based, but may be combined with other forms such as performance, painting, sculpture, film, music or literature. Photographers, artists, curators, archives and collectives worldwide may enter, aged 16 or over, with a parent or guardian's consent at 16 and 17. Each entry is either a photography project of 1 to 15 images or a photobook as a PDF proof, and an entrant may enter as many as they like — but each is a separate entry carrying its own fee.
What selection buys is scale rather than a cheque alone. Ten to fifteen artists are chosen; their work is produced as large-format prints by the festival at no cost to the artist and shown across the city of Belfast from 3 to 27 June 2027, with a partner exhibition produced by Photo Schweiz 2027, a contribution towards travel to the opening, a year of Royal Photographic Society membership, three one-to-one sessions with the curatorial team, international press coverage, and promotion to the festival's 30,000-plus social following and 13,000-plus subscribers. One selected artist takes the £2,000 Spotlight Award, which in 2026 the jury split between two photographers. The one cost that can land on a selected entrant is in the photobook route: a selected book must reach the festival professionally printed and bound by 1 May 2027, and shipping to Belfast, insurance and the cost of return are the entrant's responsibility. Shortlisted artists are contacted on 18 March 2027, results are announced in April, the festival opens on 3 June 2027, and the international portfolio reviews — which entrants get a discount on — run from 18 June.
The fee is staged, and the organiser's own surfaces disagree on when the early rung closes: the call page and the Picter listing both say £22 per entry until 11:59pm GMT on 11 December 2026, while the festival's terms and conditions say 27 November 2026 in two separate clauses. Those same terms still give 23 October 2026 as the opening date although the call in fact opened on 11 November, so 27 November is the date to beat. After the early rung it is £26 per entry until the 5 February 2027 close, and the terms reserve the right to extend that deadline. The festival states where the money goes — it is a registered charity in Northern Ireland (NIC102819) and says entry fees fund exhibition production and printing, artist travel, jury fees, the submission platform and promotion, alongside core funding from the Arts Council of Northern Ireland and Belfast City Council, with more than £100,000 invested in artists' fees since 2024. Every eligible entry is scored independently by every juror before the full jury shortlists and selects together, and the jury is published in full: Charmaine Toh of Tate Modern, Roxana Marcoci of MoMA, Alessia Glaviano of PhotoVogue, Mikko Takkunen of The New York Times, Florian Ebner of the Centre Pompidou, Laura Ligari of the International Photography Festivals Association, and festival founder Michael Weir. — Deadline: February 5, 2027. Fee: £22 per entry early bird (to 27 November 2026 in the terms, 11 December on the call page), then £26. Prize: £2,000 Spotlight Award + Exhibition.

item.title: 5th Annual Exhibition & Competition · APA New York
item.description:
The New York chapter of American Photographic Artists reaches the fifth edition of its annual juried competition, and the offer is specific: 80 photographs selected for a one-week open-gallery exhibition at Soho Photo Gallery from February 2 to 7, 2027, with a reception on February 4 and a fully illustrated show catalogue. Soho Photo was founded in 1971 by a group of New York Times photojournalists and avant-garde photographers, is New York City's longest-running co-op gallery, and now sits in Chelsea. The chapter is explicit that no genre is out of scope — personal or assignment work, commercial or fine art, reportage, fashion, street, still life, landscape, macro or portraits, “digital or old-school alternative processes”, colour or black and white, and “any photographic genre we forgot to mention”. Around the show the chapter names a feature on the APA website, social media, the catalogue, and an opening reception intended to bring in “the industry professionals who buy photographs and hire photographers”.
The curator is Elizabeth Renstrom, a New York photo editor, curator and photographer whose own work deals in nostalgia, femininity and consumer culture; she was Senior Photo Editor at The New Yorker and held editorial positions at VICE, Marie Claire and TIME. She has judged or reviewed for LensCulture, the Lucie Photo Book Awards, APA-Los Angeles, Red Hook Labs New Talent, Photoville, Belfast Photo Festival and the Daylight Photo Book Awards, and has taught at Parsons School of Design and the International Center of Photography. Curating is blind: submitted files are assigned an arbitrary ID and the photographers' names reach the curator only after selection is complete. Eighty photographs are chosen in all, one photographer cannot have more than five images in the show, and the curator may take all or any part of a series entry.
Entry is priced per image and membership halves it: $25 per image for APA members and $50 per image for non-members, the same rates for single images and for series entries of two to four images. APA membership runs across five levels starting at $50, and the competition is open to photographers whether or not they join. There is no cash prize — what is awarded is the wall, the catalogue and the reception. Files are JPEGs of up to 2MB at 1800 pixels on the long side, with no watermarks, named Lastname-Firstname-Title (series entries add -Series-XofY) and no special characters. There is no restriction on when the work was made, but an image already selected in a previous APA New York annual exhibition will not be considered, and winning images from past APA competitions are barred. AI is excluded twice over: the submission guidelines say work created using AI-generated prompts is “not considered photography for this contest”, and entrants separately warrant that their submission contains no elements created by AI.
One date needs care. The Important Dates block — on the call page and on the entry page both — gives December 3, 2026 as the submission deadline, while the Contest Terms further down the call page state that “the deadline for entries is December 1, 2026”. The chapter has not reconciled the two, so a photographer who wants certainty should be in by December 1. Winners are notified no later than December 21, 2026 and supply a high-resolution file for the book and the exhibition print by December 30. Entry fees are not refundable, entrants keep full copyright, and the permission granted to APA covers exhibition and promotion of the work with credit. — Deadline: December 3, 2026. Fee: $50 per image ($25 APA members). Prize: Group exhibition at Soho Photo Gallery, New York + illustrated show catalogue.

item.title: Photographs They Told You Not to Show · UNSTAGED
item.description:
UNSTAGED is a small publisher whose books are built as “narrative-led anthological inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity”, and its next anthology, guest-curated by Aga Łuczakowska, goes after the pictures that were kept back. The call states its own brief without softening it: “This is an open call for projects that refuse to play nice. We are looking for heavy emotional impact, noise, Images that were once hidden, censored because they crossed a line. The ones that were ‘too much.’ Too intense. Too loud. Too intimate. Too honest.” The research question set for the book is who decides what is too much to be seen, and how those lines are drawn; the approach named is critical visual research, auto-theory and visual non-fiction. The publisher hands each volume to a guest artist who sets the open-call theme and serves as guest curator, guiding the publication to its final form; as with its previous projects, the selected works are gathered into an anthology book that explores the theme through photographic inquiry — the cover image shown with the call is from the first edition of the UNSTAGED Anthology, a photograph by Ben Osborne.
There is no money in either direction: the call says “NO submission fee | NO contribution fee”, and no cash award, royalty or honorarium is mentioned — what is on offer is a place in a printed anthology. Entries are a set of 5 to 10 photographs as JPEGs with the long edge at 2000 pixels and 300 dpi (the publisher calls that resolution essential for print curation), with black-and-white images supplied in grayscale colour mode, plus a project description of up to 500 words. Files must be named Name_Project Title_01 and uploaded to a Google Drive folder set to public access, with the project description inside the folder, preferably as a PDF; the folder link is then sent to the publisher's own submission address. Emails with files attached directly are not considered.
One clause is worth reading before writing the description: AI-assisted text editing is permitted, but the publisher says it will reject descriptions “dominated by generic AI language and lacking the artist's own autobiographical/auto-theoretical/research-based perspective”. That sentence is about the writing, not the photographs, and the call states no policy on AI-generated images. The deadline is December 6 at 23:59 AoE — Anywhere on Earth, the latest timezone on the planet — so the cutoff is a full day later than a UTC reading of the date suggests. Note that the publisher's own shop and open-calls pages at un-staged.com are behind a password at the moment, so the call post on its own Instagram account is the live surface for this edition. — Deadline: December 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Manuscrypt Magazine — Winter Horror · Cult Publishing
item.description:
Cult Publishing is a small horror press that describes the publishing world as "a sucking void of unanswered and untapped talent" and itself as "the void answering back", existing to platform emerging voices whose work is undeservedly unseen. Its magazine, Manuscrypt, is built around a binding theme each issue, and art submissions are open for the next one: Winter Horror. The press asks for work that encapsulates the horror of the winter season — its own prompts are blood on fresh snow, figures in the gale, bodies frozen mid-scream in ice, trees devoid of green. Fitting the theme is not mandatory, but themed work is favoured for acceptance.
Photography is named first among the accepted media — "art submitted to the magazine can be photography, digital art, and drawings, but we are not limited to these mediums" — and the magazine's FAQ repeats it. Both original and reprinted art are accepted for this issue. There is no submission fee and no payment step anywhere in the route, and every accepted submission is paid $50 — but the organiser's two surfaces disagree about reprints. The website FAQ says "at this time, we do not pay for reprints", while the submission form itself promises "$50.00 for all successful original and reprinted art submissions"; the form asks each entrant to mark the piece Original or Reprint, so a reprint may still fall under the FAQ's exclusion. Original work that is accepted carries three months' exclusivity from publication and First Publication Rights pass to the magazine, a point Cult Publishing spells out at length and links to Clarkesworld editor Neil Clarke's guide and the Society of Authors' contract guidance rather than burying. Simultaneous submissions are accepted; the FAQ asks for one story per writer per issue, and the art form takes a single title and one file per submission.
Work goes through a Google Form as a PDF or image file of up to 100 MB, at a minimum of 300 dpi; the magazine page is 8.5 by 11 inches but the art does not have to match that. The form uploads the file to Google Drive, so a Google account is needed to attach it, and it heads itself "Winter Edition" where the call page names the theme Winter Horror. AI is refused without qualification: "We do not publish work generated by AI in any form. Whether it is text, images, or otherwise." Submissions opened on 28 October 2026 and close at 5pm EST on Friday 20 November 2026, with every entrant answered after the window shuts. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $50 per accepted work + publication.

item.title: Lightvisions · Photo Artfolio
item.description:
Photo Artfolio returns to the theme of its inaugural exhibit with a new round of Lightvisions, a global online exhibition about the expressive power of light. The call asks for photographs in which light is essential to the image's impact — the organiser's own examples are a face lit by a flickering screen, hard sunlight cutting across an empty street, the glow of a carefully lit still life, and an ordinary space made unfamiliar by reflections and shadow. Work that finds something unexpected in available light is welcomed alongside work built through deliberate lighting and experimentation, and the call is open to all photographic genres and approaches: documentary, portraiture, street, landscape, nature, architecture, still life, conceptual, fine art and experimental photography, in colour and in black and white alike.
Entry is open to photographers worldwide, with amateur and professional photographers both encouraged to apply. Up to 20 images may be submitted, at $20 for the first image and $5 for each additional one; fees are non-refundable and do not guarantee acceptance. Files are JPEG only, a minimum of 1,200 pixels on the longest side and no more than 5 MB. All work must be original and made by the submitting photographer, and AI-generated imagery is not eligible.
Cash awards of $500, $350 and $150 go to the top three images, and every accepted photograph is shown in the online exhibition, which opens on the same day the results are announced. Photographers keep full copyright; submitting grants Photo Artfolio permission to show accepted images on its website, social channels and promotional material, with credit where feasible. Sales enquiries are passed to the photographer's own website and the photographer receives the whole of any resulting sale — the platform takes no commission. Submissions are reviewed by Creative Director Julia Cumes with an anonymous committee of jurors, and results are emailed on 3 February 2027 to the address on the entrant's CaFE account. The entry window closes at 11:59pm MST on 13 January 2027. — Deadline: January 13, 2027. Fee: $20 + $5 each additional image. Prize: $500 + $350 + $150 + Online exhibition.

item.title: Beyond the Horizon · Gulf Coast Artists' Alliance
item.description:
GCAA ArtWorks, the storefront gallery and studio space of the Gulf Coast Artists' Alliance at 5546 1st Ave. N. in St. Petersburg, opens its new year with a themed juried show. "Beyond the Horizon" is put as "a metaphor for what lies past your immediate vision, knowledge, and comfort zone" — limitless potential, hope, ambition and growth — and the gallery asks artists to "interpret the theme as you like and depict your vision for the New Year". The application states that a loose interpretation of the theme will be accepted, and that all media are eligible, sculpture included. No surface names photography specifically; what does is the gallery's own online shop, which sells eleven photographs under a Photography/Digital Art heading at $145 to $240.
Up to three works per artist are considered for a single non-refundable $20 jury fee. Applying takes two separate actions and the gallery says so twice: you click Submit Application on the form, then Pay Jury Fee Here, a Square checkout whose own item page states that payment does not guarantee inclusion in an exhibition. Wall work is capped at 30x40 inches, sculpture at roughly 48 inches tall by 18 wide by 18 deep. Entry images are uploaded through the form on the call page as JPEG or PNG files of about 1200x1000 pixels, named with your surname and the title of the work — the gallery says low-resolution files will be rejected — alongside the title, medium, size and retail price of each piece and an artist's statement of up to 300 words; a CV upload is optional. Work sent from out of town is accepted provided a return shipping label comes with it.
The exhibition runs 7 January - 6 February 2027 with a reception on Saturday 9 January during the Second Saturday Art Walk in downtown St. Pete. Selected artists are emailed the rest of the show guidelines by 18 December 2026. Sales are handled by the gallery, which takes 35 per cent commission from GCAA members and 40 per cent from non-members. No cash award is attached to this call. — Deadline: December 13, 2026. Fee: $20 (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Color: Emotion. Story. Metaphor. · Black Eyes Gallery
item.description:
The January show at Black Eyes Gallery, a submission-based photography and fine-art gallery at 485 S. Stone Avenue in Tucson, is about colour doing the work: "The tone of an entire photograph can be changed simply by the color of the lighting: the blue-green of fluorescent, or the warm glow of incandescent. Nothing in the frame moves. Only the color does." Any genre — landscape, street, portrait, experimental, conceptual — and any colour process, film, digital or alternative. Images with selective colour are eligible; black-and-white and monochrome work is not, and belongs in the gallery's separate monochrome call.
Twenty-five images are selected and the gallery prints, mats and frames every one at its own cost, so there is nothing to produce or ship. One exhibition print is made; the gallery holds it in its archive for two years and then destroys it. Selected work hangs 2–30 January 2027 with an opening reception on 2 January, 5–8pm, enters the gallery's permanent online exhibition archive with the artist's name, title and social link, and is promoted across the gallery's channels including a feature on its Instagram. The juror is Douglas Fur, a Tucson photographer with a BFA from Cornish College of the Arts who has worked at Decode Gallery and is gallery manager and artist liaison for Tucson Erotica. Review is blind wherever possible — the gallery says a CV and bio will most likely not factor into selection.
Open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over, except where US sanctions or payment-processing rules stop the gallery accepting a submission. Entry is $40 for up to five images or $50 for up to ten, paid on the JotForm entry form; a reduced $20 fee is available to two artists per call, first come, if you contact the gallery before submitting, and an entry with nothing selected earns $5 off the next. Listing work for sale is optional and encouraged, with the gallery suggesting $200–$500 and retaining 50 per cent on gallery sales — the entry form asks you to acknowledge that split. Work made entirely or substantially with AI is disqualified. Files are JPEGs, at least 1200px on the long side, named lastname_firstname_title. Artists keep full copyright; the gallery takes a non-exclusive right to reproduce selected images for jurying, the exhibition, its archive and promotion. — Deadline: December 18, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 5 images) / $50 (up to 10); $20 reduced fee for two artists per call. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Sparkplug Artists' Collective · DC Arts Center
item.description:
The Sparkplug Artists' Collective is the DC Arts Center's one-year programme for artists seeking to establish, reignite or sustain a professional art career. Around ten artists are chosen each year through an application and interview process, from deliberately wide-ranging backgrounds and levels of experience. Members meet monthly for studio visits, moderated peer critiques and social events, with art excursions and workshops alongside — and, crucially, exhibition opportunities in the centre's own galleries in Adams Morgan, Washington DC.
DCAC has two renovated spaces: the Main Gallery, about 700 square feet, which takes full-size work in all media, and the 125-square-foot Nano Gallery for small-format work. Artists keep 60 per cent of the price of anything sold, or 70 per cent for DCAC Artist Members. The centre states that it accepts applications from all artists working seriously in their field and does not discriminate on any basis; note that the programme itself runs in person in Washington DC, with monthly meetings and studio visits through the year, and that the collective has so far drawn its nearly 100 members from the greater Washington, D.C., area.
Applications ask for an artist statement and biography, a résumé and work samples from the last five years, current or past. There is a $25 application fee and a $250 programme cost, both waived for DCAC Artist Members. Applications close at 11:59 PM on 29 November 2026; shortlisted candidates are interviewed after the deadline, decisions are communicated in December, and the 2027 cohort runs from 1 January to 31 December 2027. — Deadline: November 29, 2026. Fee: $25 ($250 programme cost if selected; both waived for members). Prize: Exhibition + Mentorship.

item.title: 2027 Winter Art Show · Paul Nigra Center for Creative Arts
item.description:
The Paul Nigra Center for Creative Arts is a community arts centre in Gloversville, in upstate New York, founded in 2015 by Lexington, an accredited provider of disability services in New York State. It mounts several open shows a year — Winter, Regional, New York State Summer, Membership and Reflection — and hosts an annual exhibition of the Adirondack Life magazine photography contest winners. For the 2027 Winter Art Show it invites artists everywhere to submit work in any medium: celebrate the new year with new art, or show older work to a new audience.
Entry is through OnlineJuriedShows. Up to three works cost $25, or $15 for centre members, with additional entries at $10 each ($7 for members) to a maximum of five. Work must be original in both design and personal execution, and anything previously shown at the centre is not eligible. Hanging works must weigh no more than 25 pounds including frame and hardware, and selected pieces must arrive suitably framed and ready to install. The centre does not accept content involving nudity or sexual themes, citing the range of ages and cultures among its regular visitors.
Acceptances are emailed by 6 January 2027 and selected work is received at the centre between 13 and 16 January, either in person or shipped at the artist's expense with a $10 handling fee per package. The exhibition runs from 22 January to 25 March 2027, with a public opening reception on Thursday 28 January, 4–7pm; awards are chosen and announced on 27 January. The centre retains a 20 per cent commission on sales, and unsold work left uncollected 60 days after the close is forfeited. — Deadline: January 3, 2027. Fee: $25 for up to 3 works ($15 members); $10 each additional ($7 members), max 5. Prize: Exhibition + Awards.

item.title: Magnum Opus 2027 · Sacramento Fine Arts Center
item.description:
Magnum Opus is the Sacramento Fine Arts Center's premier annual juried show — the centre defines a magnum opus as an important work of art and asks artists to enter the most outstanding thing they have made recently. It is open to all media, and photography is accommodated by an explicit exception rather than by omission: the rules bar copies, giclées and enhanced giclées and "works by any commercial printing process (except for photography)", so photographic prints are eligible where other printed reproductions are not. Class and workshop art, crafts and copyrighted works are excluded, as is anything already shown in a juried show at Sac Arts.
Work must be original and finished within the last three years, must be exactly as presented in the online entry, and must be listed for sale — the centre retains a 50% commission on sales for non-members and 30% for members, so prices should be set accordingly. Two-dimensional pieces should not exceed 40 lb or measure more than 4 × 8 feet; anything larger than 29 × 35 inches must be glazed with plastic rather than glass. Hanging work must have clean edges and be framed unless it is three-dimensional, canvases under three-quarter gallery wrap must be framed, and every hanging piece must be wired with D-rings only, wire ends taped, with no protruding nails, staples or sawtooth hangers. The artist's name, address, phone, email, title, size, media and price go on the back of 2-D work and on the back or base of 3-D work.
Entry is through Artwork Archive at $25 per work for a maximum of three pieces, with a 20% discount for members, whose codes are sent out by email and phone. Staff will also enter work on an artist's behalf in person at no additional cost by appointment, though appointments are not accepted on the day of the deadline. Awards carry a cash prize for every awarded work, and Best of Show may receive a solo exhibit at the centre in 2028. The 2027 judge is Jenny Williams, a native Californian painter who studied studio art at Brunel University in London and holds a BA in Design Studies from San Francisco State University; she works in an American Impressionist, largely plein-air idiom, teaches fine art to children and youth with special needs, and belongs to the Women's Caucus for Art and the American Impressionist Society. Entries close on 19 January 2027 at 11:59pm, acceptances go out on 29 January, work is received on 13 February by appointment, and the exhibition runs 16 February to 13 March 2027 at the centre in Carmichael, with a closing reception on 13 March from 5 to 7pm and pick-up straight afterwards. Shipped work must arrive no later than the receiving date, and the artist initiates and pays for all shipping. The show chair is Paul Dessau. — Deadline: January 19, 2027. Fee: $25 per work, up to 3 works (20% member discount). Prize: Cash prize for every awarded work + possible solo exhibition in 2028 for Best of Show.

item.title: Open Call: Exhibitions 2028 — Metamorphosis · MUU Helsinki Contemporary Art Centre
item.description:
MUU Helsinki Contemporary Art Centre, run by the Artists' Association MUU — a national interdisciplinary organisation founded in 1987 that represents and promotes new media art in Finland — invites professional artists, artist groups and curators to propose an exhibition or a multi-artistic event for its 2028 programme. The centre occupies 160 square metres at the Cable Factory in Helsinki's Ruoholahti, one of the largest cultural centres in the country, and its audiences run daily from families with children to senior citizens. Exhibition periods in 2028 generally last four to five weeks, and the MUU selection committee informs every applicant of the result.
The theme for 2028 is Metamorphosis — to change form, to become something different. MUU frames it as a change that can be sudden and visible or so gradual it goes unnoticed, in nature, geology, myth and story alike, and asks what actually changes when something takes a new form: what shifts within us and around us, what emerges, disappears or remains. The call is explicitly open to unforeseeable alteration and to the slow emergence of the new rather than to a single reading of the word.
MUU pays the artists and groups who exhibit there. The fee depends on the number of participating artists, the duration of the event and the size of the space used, and the 2028 levels will be confirmed by early 2028; for comparison, in 2026 a four- to five-week solo exhibition paid between €2,290 and €2,700 per artist. Exhibitors have full use of the centre's presentation technology, and a floor plan and technical specification are published alongside the call. Artists remain responsible for the production costs of their works and for transport, insurance, travel, accommodation and similar expenses.
Applications go through MUU's online form by 18 November 2026 at 18:00 (UTC+02:00) and ask for a one-page CV, a 500–1,000 character biography of the artist or group, a project plan of up to 2,000 characters, and a single image file of no more than 5 MB in PNG, JPG or PDF (multiple images must be combined into one file). Applicants also describe in up to 2,000 characters how they intend to use the exhibition space, with a floor plan recommended, explain in up to 1,000 characters each how the proposal relates to the theme and to the other activities at the Cable Factory, and state whether the exhibition is a premiere or where and when it has been shown before. Links to video or audio works, with any passwords, may be added. — Deadline: November 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + artist fee (€2,290–€2,700 per artist for a 4–5 week solo show in 2026; 2028 levels confirmed in early 2028).

item.title: Anja Niedringhaus Courage in Photojournalism Award 2027 · International Women's Media Foundation
item.description: The IWMF's award for courageous, high-impact photojournalism by women, nonbinary and gender nonconforming photojournalists, created in 2014 with a $1 million gift from the Howard G. Buffett Foundation to honour Anja Niedringhaus, the Pulitzer Prize-winning Associated Press photographer killed in 2014 while covering the elections in Afghanistan. The IWMF frames it as celebrating visual journalistic work that inspires us to take action and compels us to better understand the world. One winner receives a cash prize of $20,000, is publicly honoured and has the work showcased. Entry is free. An application consists of candidate information, a work sample of twelve photographs that best represent the scope and style of the candidate's work in challenging reporting environments — six of which must have been made between 2024 and 2026 — and a candidate statement. Both freelancers and photojournalists affiliated with media organisations are eligible, but journalism must be the candidate's full-time primary profession. A photographer may self-nominate or be nominated by an editor, mentor or journalist peer; a third party can either file a full application or complete an abbreviated nomination form, which does not replace the full submission. Submissions for the 2027 cycle opened 10 November 2026 and close 1 April 2027 at 03:59 UTC, which is 31 March in the Americas, and the IWMF states the winner will be announced in summer 2027. The 2026 awardee was Nicole Tung, with honourable mentions to Daro Sulakauri and Viviana Peretti. The IWMF's own pages have not been rolled forward for this cycle: the award page still presents the 2026 honorees, and the application guidelines and FAQ still read 2026 throughout — the FAQ states the application is open until 31 March 2026, the third-party nomination form carries the same 2026 date, and the recency rule is printed as 2024-2026, which is also the window the organiser's own 2027 submission record repeats. The 2027 dates are published only on that record. The terms are strict on authenticity: photographs must not be manipulated beyond basic colour and contrast correction and minor lightness and darkness adjustments, the IWMF may ask finalists or the winner for the original RAW camera files, and the award follows the NPPA code of ethics. Alongside the summer 2027 wording, the submission platform's timeline also lists 30 September 2027 as the results announcement date. — Deadline: March 31, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $20,000.

item.title: GLIMMER — 2027 Elizabeth Richard Memorial Members' Show · East End Arts Council
item.description: The first exhibition of East End Arts Council's year and its annual members' show, held in the council's downtown galleries at 48 and 11 West Main Street in Riverhead, New York, from 23 January to 27 February 2027. The 2027 theme is GLIMMER, an exploration and celebration of light in all its forms — from shimmer, reflection and radiance to glow, shadow and illumination — and the council invites artists to consider how light influences what we see, what we feel and how we experience the world around us, interpreted literally, symbolically or abstractly. Member artists of all disciplines may submit one original artwork; painting, photography, sculpture, mixed media and other disciplines are all named as welcome. The show is non-juried, so there is no selection panel, though the council reserves the right to request an alternative piece if it feels a work does not suitably meet the theme. Participation is open to East End Arts Council members with active memberships — individual membership starts at $45 a year on the council's own membership page — and the submission fee on top of that is $5, which the organisers say helps cover administrative and installation costs. Entry is through the council's own online submission form, which doubles as the loan sheet and carries the full consignment terms: work must be ready for installation on delivery, the artist is responsible for transporting it to and from the gallery at their own expense, no additional fine art insurance is provided, and on a sale the artist chooses in advance between taking 70 percent, taking 50 percent, or donating the whole amount to the council. Submissions opened 12 October 2026 and close 3 January 2027; selected work must be dropped off no later than 9 January, with artists contacted about drop-off or shipping, and the opening reception is on 23 January 2027. Unsold work must be collected within 14 days of the exhibition closing, and the loan sheet states that work left beyond 90 days is considered a donation to the council and becomes its property. — Deadline: January 3, 2027. Fee: $5 (EEAC membership required). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: IN OUR TIME 2027 · Sussex Contemporary
item.description: Sussex Contemporary's contemporary response to the Bayeux Tapestry: a collective portrait of life in 2027, made by UK and French artists and shown at The Atrium, Marine Workshops, Newhaven, from 21 August to 12 September 2027 with free public admission. The brief is deliberately open — a personal experience, a public event, a community, a concern, a celebration or an everyday observation; the organisers state the work need not depict the Tapestry or Norman history at all, and "we're leaving the narrative to you". Like the organisation's PASSAGE call this is what Sussex Contemporary calls a democratic exhibition: the FAQ states plainly "There is no selection panel or competitive judging", and entry guarantees inclusion provided the finished work meets the published requirements and arrives by the delivery deadline. The format is the constraint, and it is tight: every contributor works on the same supplied A5 canvas-covered board (148 × 210mm, portrait orientation), unframed, with a maximum total depth of 1cm including any raised elements, and the works hang in one continuous line with no gaps between them. Three-dimensional work is excluded for that reason. Participation is £40, which covers the board, guaranteed inclusion, a listing in the printed and online catalogues and a private view invitation for two on 21 August 2027; board collection from Seawhite's showroom in Partridge Green is free, and delivery and return postage are optional extras of £3 to £14.50 depending on whether the board goes to a UK or French address and whether unsold work is posted back. Sending the finished artwork to Sussex Contemporary is arranged and paid for by the artist. All work must be for sale and stays up until the exhibition closes; artists set their own price, receive 70 percent and the organisation retains 30 percent commission including VAT, with payment for sold work made on 1 October 2027. Entries close 9 July 2027 at 23:59 UK time, catalogue information is due by 22 July and completed artwork must arrive by 30 July. The guarantee has a limit the call page does not print. The linked terms and conditions, which are the binding document, reserve to Sussex Contemporary the right to accept or decline any work submitted entirely at its discretion, with its decision final, and to withdraw a work whose display could expose the organisation to reputational or legal risk. The same terms extend the 30 percent commission to any sale made within three months of the exhibition closing as a result of the display, charge £15 per week per work for late collection, and treat a work not removed within 28 days of the final collection date as abandoned, which allows Sussex Contemporary to sell or dispose of it without notifying the artist. Unsold work can be collected at Marine Workshops on Monday 13 September 2027 between 10am and 3pm. Submitting grants the organisation an irrevocable, royalty-free consent in perpetuity to reproduce the work for promotion, press, signage and catalogue use. French entrants should note that return postage covers a packed work of up to 500g, above which the organisers ask to be contacted before entering, and that any import taxes are the artist's. — Deadline: July 9, 2027. Fee: £40 (+£3-£14.50 optional postage). Prize: Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: 2027 Foto Forum Santa Fe Photography Award
item.description:
Foto Forum Santa Fe's annual international award is built around a solo exhibition rather than a group hang.
