The first-place photographer receives a two-month solo show in the gallery's space in the Railyard Art District, down the street from SITE Santa Fe, a $1,000 cash prize, and a $500 stipend towards delivering the work to the gallery and having it returned. The 2027 juror is Leigh Ledare, whose work on agency, intimacy and consent is held by the Museum of Modern Art, the Art Institute of Chicago, MOCA Los Angeles, the Centre Pompidou and Fotomuseum Winterthur, and who held a Guggenheim Fellowship in 2017.
The call is open internationally to emerging and established artists. Photographers submit up to twelve photographs from a related body of work that is ready for exhibition, each file between 1 MB and 2 MB. The organisation asks for a cohesive selection rather than a survey of everything an applicant makes, and suggests the artist statement explain how the twelve images relate to each other. Video submissions are not accepted, though video can form part of the resulting exhibition; applicants with video work may submit stills and describe the piece in the statement. The winner then works with executive director Sage Paisner to curate the final show, which may include work not submitted with the application.
Entries are read by the outside juror and by Paisner as in-house curator. The organisation notes that artists who entered without winning have been added to the gallery roster. Past winners are Jared Ragland, Federico Estol, Rebecca Moseman, Ciro Battiloro, Jerry Takigawa and Renee Romero. Jury selection begins 15 March 2027, results are announced and the winner contacted on 18 April 2027, and the solo exhibition opens with a reception on 4 June 2027.
The entry fee rises in stages: $40 from the opening on 10 November 2026 until 22 January 2027, $50 from 23 January to 24 February, and $60 from 25 February until the 4 March close at midnight Mountain Time. Students, seniors and members can email the gallery for a 20% discount coupon. Foto Forum Santa Fe is a non-profit space programming exhibitions, workshops, visiting artist lectures and community outreach around photography, storytelling, science and technology. — Deadline: March 4, 2027. Fee: $40 early bird until Jan 22, then $50 until Feb 24, $60 late entry; 20% student/senior/member discount on request. Prize: $1,000 + $500 shipping + Solo exhibition.

item.title: ART OF THE STILL LIFE · MVA Gallery
item.description:
MVA Gallery, a commercial gallery in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, runs a rolling programme of themed national group shows, and this one takes the still life. The brief is deliberately wide. The gallery notes that past centuries favoured flowers, fruit, plants, vases, books, candles, shells, mirrors, plates and musical instruments, often loaded with symbolic or moralistic meaning, but it invites work built from anything, however mundane — a pot, a toaster, a clock, a phone, a computer, a lamp, clothing, jewellery, toys. Objects can be presented in their natural state or, through artistic manipulation, debased or elevated. All styles and techniques are welcome, from a straightforward image to an openly experimental one.
The gallery shows painting, watercolour, printmaking, mixed media, digital, pastel, encaustic, ink, sculpture, fibre, drawing and photography, and all photographic processes are welcome. Photographs should be framed for a traditional presentation, with black or white frames preferred and white or off-white mats where used, though other mounting is considered. There is no cut-off date for when the work was made. Entry is $35 for three different images, $5 for each additional file up to nine. Work is reviewed by a small rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers, curators and academics, who have asked to remain anonymous.
Three awards are in play. An Art of Distinction award selects one artist for a featured show in the gallery's Exhibition Room Two at a future date. The Director's Choice Award is $200, granted at the executive director's discretion. The annual Grand Prize goes to one artist chosen from everyone exhibited at MVA across the calendar year, who is offered an exhibition opportunity in New York City and notified in December. The jurors reserve the right not to award any or all prizes.
Notification is on or about 12 March 2027 by email, accepted work must reach the gallery by 30 April 2027, and the exhibition runs 5 to 30 May 2027. Artists pay shipping and insurance both ways and must enclose a prepaid return UPS or FedEx label. Framed work should not exceed 48 inches on the longest side or 45 lbs; plexiglass is strongly preferred over glass for shipped pieces. Sales are optional, must list a specific price, and are split 70% to the artist and 30% to the gallery. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: PORTALS, PASSAGES, AND BEYOND · MVA Gallery
item.description:
A national group show at MVA Gallery in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, on the threshold as subject. Portals — doors, entranceways, windows — work as physical and psychological points of arrival and departure. The gallery writes that doors may be admired for their architectural features but can also be symbolic, and that windows reveal atmospheric views while carrying factual or metaphorical meaning. The theme extends to corridors, streets, tunnels and bridges, which can serve as symbolic entrances into other realms, real or imaginary. The question the call puts is what lies beyond: a crossing into a mysterious or spiritual experience, or into a macabre, happy or dreamed reality.
Both registers are wanted. A straightforward image of a portal or passageway is as welcome as one layered with symbolic associations. The gallery shows painting, watercolour, printmaking, mixed media, digital, pastel, encaustic, ink, sculpture, fibre, drawing and photography, and all photographic processes are welcome. Photographs should be framed for a traditional presentation — black or white frames preferred, white or off-white mats only where used — though other mounting is considered. No cut-off applies to when the work was made. Entry is $35 for three different images and $5 for each additional file up to nine. A small rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers and academics evaluates the work and has asked to remain anonymous.
An Art of Distinction award is granted at most exhibitions: one artist is selected by the jurors and featured in a special show in the gallery's Exhibition Room Two at a future date. The Director's Choice Award is $200 at the executive director's discretion, and the annual Grand Prize offers one artist from everyone exhibited at MVA during the calendar year an exhibition opportunity in New York City, with notification in December. The jurors reserve the right not to award any or all prizes.
Notification is on or about 19 March 2027 by email, accepted work must arrive by 30 April 2027, and the exhibition runs 5 to 30 May 2027. Artists cover shipping and insurance in both directions and must enclose a prepaid return UPS or FedEx label. Framed work should stay under 48 inches on the longest side and 45 lbs, and plexiglass is preferred to glass for anything shipped. Sales are optional, must list a specific price, and are split 70% to the artist and 30% to the gallery. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: photoED Magazine — Objects (Issue #79)
item.description:
photoED, the Canadian photography magazine, is building Issue #79 around still life: photographers exploring objects with unique, lens-based methods. The call asks for fine art photography projects that present objects in unusual compositions — the magazine's own framing runs from the historic repertoire of flowers, fruit, plants, vases, books, candles, shells, mirrors, plates and musical instruments to anything mundane that an artist's eye picks out. What it does not want is stock photography, and it does not want commissions: existing projects and finished works only.
The editors ask for well considered submissions — a project or idea that has been laboured over — and diverse interpretations of the theme. Entries are blind reviewed by the magazine's volunteer curatorial editorial board, and judges assess how the work presents a unique reading of the subject rather than how technically polished a single frame is. The magazine recommends reading a full print or digital replica of a recent edition before submitting, to work out whether the work is a fit.
Entry is limited to eight images and one submission per person. Files should be at least 2000 pixels on the longest side and no larger than 10 MB each, and every filename must carry the photographer's first and last name. Submitting transfers no rights: the photographer keeps full ownership, the magazine asks for no exclusivity, and the same images can go to any other publication, project or exhibition.
Selected contributors are published in photoED's print and digital replica editions, and those chosen for print receive printed copies with worldwide shipping. Additional selected contributors may feature in the free-access Digital Extra companion editions, and all contributors are promoted across the magazine's email campaigns and social channels. Entry is free for paid Patreon patrons and paid print subscribers, who also receive a copy of the edition automatically when it appears in April 2027; the general fee is $20 CAD, or $30 within Canada and $35 internationally if an entrant opts to pre-purchase a single print copy as part of the fee. All entrants may opt in to free digital replica access. The editor will waive the fee for economically challenged artists on request. Entries are welcome worldwide, with the exception of residents of Russia, Belarus and sanctioned countries. — Deadline: February 19, 2027. Fee: $20 CAD (subscribers and Patreon patrons free). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Fully Subsidised Scheme — Free Studio and Darkroom Access · Photosynthesis NZ
item.description:
Photosynthesis, the non-profit that runs a community photography studio and darkroom in Ōtautahi Christchurch, covers the full cost of its space and equipment for qualifying projects. The scheme is funded by the Rātā Foundation and grew out of a 2023 pilot. Its current document covers 2025/26 and states that it is open for applications, with no closing date.
The subsidy covers every cost of using the studio and darkroom and their equipment, for shooting, workshops, meetings, mentoring or learning, as long as the use belongs to the approved project. Participants receive keys, against a one-time bond, and can use the spaces 24 hours a day, seven days a week, booked through the organisation's portal and subject to availability. Photosynthesis finds mentors for the project and pays them. Nothing else is funded: artist fees, printing, publication and exhibition costs stay with the artist, who may look for outside funding.
Projects are judged on four criteria. The work gives a voice to people traditionally under-represented in fine art, such as sexual and gender minorities, ethnic and cultural minorities, and disabled and elderly communities. It could not go ahead without the subsidy. It needs the studio and equipment many times, not once. It ends in published work an audience can see, such as a book or zine, an exhibition of prints or a video online. The scheme is for local artists. Past projects include Life/Styles 2024, a photographic archive made with young people from across the city and shown at Tūranga library, and Mau Rākau, a book and exhibition about practitioners of Māori weaponry.
Applicants fill in an expression-of-interest form covering who is involved, the project's length and output, its current status and how it meets the criteria. Staff then arrange a meeting at the studio and work through approval with the applicant. There is no formal reporting. Projects that do not qualify may be offered reduced non-commercial rates instead. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Fully subsidised studio and darkroom access + paid mentors.

item.title: Dummy Award 2027 · The PhotoBookMuseum
item.description: The international competition for the best unpublished photobook dummies of the year, now in its 17th edition. The Kassel Fotobook Festival began inviting photographers to the Kassel Dummy Award in 2010; since 2023 The PhotoBookMuseum in Cologne has run it, with MAS Matbaa in Istanbul — the Turkish photobook printing and binding house — as printing and publishing partner. The organisers describe the rules as easy: all photographers worldwide are invited, and from all entries around 50 books are selected for a shortlist that is exhibited at international photography events. Each exhibiting venue holds a vote, decided either by public vote or by curator's choice, and those votes are combined with the shortlist jury's to select five winning books. The book that wins the PBM/MAS Prize is produced and published by MAS Matbaa in cooperation with The PhotoBookMuseum with costs fully covered; the other four winning books receive a production grant towards printing at MAS Matbaa. Every submitted book enters the Dummy Award Library and becomes part of the permanent book collection of The PhotoBookMuseum in Cologne. The organisers note that participating photographers have been able to establish contacts with galleries, publishers and festivals and to present their books to an international audience, and that hundreds of shortlisted books have been exhibited at photography events and exhibition spaces worldwide. An unpublished book, per the FAQ, is one not published by a publisher, normally without an ISBN and without distribution — a book self-published in a print run of up to 100 copies, or published digitally, still counts as unpublished and is eligible even if it has an ISBN. The definition of a photobook is given as a nonperiodic collection of photographs printed or reproduced on photographic paper, with any amount of text or even empty pages, and some form of binding. Registration runs from 3 November 2026 to 31 January 2027 through the award's own site, with a €44 entry fee paid at registration, where entrants also supply the information about their dummy. The €44 includes 7% VAT and the registration page states it is "plus shipping": entering means posting a physical book to Cologne at the entrant's own cost, and the dummy has to arrive by 17 February 2027 — a second and harder date than the registration deadline. The surfaces disagree on that deadline: the call page banner and the FAQ both close registration on 31 January 2027, while the linked terms say it "closes on the 30th of January 2027", so treat the earlier date as the real one. There is no limit on the number of entries per person, at €44 per entry and book. Three further costs fall on the entrant after submission. Books are not returned by default — every registered dummy enters the Dummy Award Library for good, and a return has to be requested when registering and paid for by the entrant 6 to 8 weeks after the March 2027 jury session, at the organiser's own estimates of €15 within Germany, €22 in the EU, €36 elsewhere in Europe and €52 worldwide for a parcel up to 2 kg. A shortlisted entrant must send a second copy of the dummy to Cologne within 21 days of the shortlist announcement, again at their own cost, or the book is left out of the overlapping exhibitions. And the PBM/MAS Prize winner waives any claim to royalties from sales and to licence revenue from the first trade edition in return for production, project management and sales being covered, instead receiving 10% of the print run to use freely and the option to buy more copies at production cost plus shipping; MAS Matbaa and the museum also reserve the right, in close consultation with the photographer, to set the print run and to change size and features to optimise production. The other four winners' grant is 25% of production and only applies if they print at MAS Matbaa. The museum says it handles dummies with the utmost care but is not liable for damage, loss or theft during the transports and exhibitions: a registration-number sticker goes inside the cover or sleeve, and a small hole may be punched in the back or cover so a cord can be attached at venues that have to secure the books. Entrants transfer a right of selective publication in the museum's and MAS Matbaa's online media with no obligation to remunerate, and cannot influence how their work is reproduced in the catalogue, the shortlist exhibitions or online; copyright otherwise stays with the author. The shortlist jury — 5 to 7 international experts, brought to Cologne for a two-day session — is announced in mid-December 2026 and meets in early March 2027, with the shortlist announced shortly after and the world tour of around 18 venues and festivals in 15 countries starting in April 2027; the five winners are announced in February 2028 on the terms page and March 2028 in the FAQ. The PhotoBookMuseum gGmbH is a non-profit, part-funded by the city of Cologne, and reports around 385 paying registrations last year. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: €44. Prize: Publication + production grants.

item.title: Solo Exhibition Series · Atlanta Photography Group
item.description: Rolling call for solo exhibition proposals at Atlanta Photography Group, the member-based photography gallery in Ansley Mall, Atlanta. Through the Solo Exhibition Series, artists of all experience levels work with APG's staff to organise and present a curated show in the Maloof Gallery: solo exhibitions alternate with group exhibitions there, each running five weeks, and four to five solo shows are presented each year. Exhibiting solo artists receive an $800 stipend, generously funded by the artist Beth Lilly. All APG members may submit proposals; solo and group proposals of lens-based work are welcome, with group proposals for up to two artists. At least half of the work submitted for review must be from the last eight years (2017 or later), exhibitions must be installed in under three days, and proposals should be made in consideration of the Maloof Gallery space — the gallery publishes its wall dimensions and encourages applicants to visit before applying. Installation work is welcome but must be approved and installed by the artist. A proposal is two documents: a text PDF describing the proposed exhibition, with a clear thesis statement, a description of the work and a timeline, noting any portion to be created on site, plus a CV of one page maximum per person; and an image PDF of up to 20 images, one per page, each captioned with artist, title, medium, dimensions and year, under 50MB in total, with links for online streaming in place of stills for video or audio work. The gallery notes that many factors influence which proposals are selected, that the programme is intended to provide career development and experience for visual artists, and that a successful proposal considers its unique multi-functional space and engages the audience visually and conceptually. The $40 proposal fee is paid through the gallery's shop, and because only members may submit, the real floor is that fee plus APG membership, priced on the gallery's own membership page at $25 a year for students and $55 for an individual, rising to $90 for a couple, $100 professional, $180 darkroom and $250 to $1,000 for the Silver, Gold and Platinum tiers. No juror is named for the series. There is no fixed deadline — once a proposal is submitted it goes on file and is considered each quarter when exhibitions are being planned, and resubmission is only needed if the exhibition idea changes. APG is funded by the City of Atlanta Mayor's Office of Cultural Affairs, Fulton County Board of Commissioners and the Georgia Council for the Arts. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: $40 + APG membership (from $25/year). Prize: $800 stipend + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Life Framer — Animal Kingdom
item.description: The January round of Life Framer's twelve-part monthly photography award. The brief asks for animal life in every register: exotic or domestic, wild or tamed, out in nature or sharing our urban spaces, thriving or merely surviving — animals as wildlife, as companions and as commodities. Life Framer asks entrants to show the creatures that share our planet, and welcomes wildlife, studio, documentary, storytelling, conceptual, candid and staged approaches from all genres and all types of photographer, with new images or work pulled from the archive. The judge for this round has not yet been announced; Life Framer prints "Judge: TBA" against the competition while naming the judges of its November and December rounds. The award is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Entry is priced by the number of images: $20 for one image into a competition of your choice, $30 for three images across one or more monthly competitions, $40 for six, or a $100 membership that covers up to ten images in every monthly themed competition for the next twelve months with no further payment. Each monthly round carries a $2,000 first prize, part of the $24,000 in cash prizes Life Framer awards across the year, and the organisers advertise four international exhibitions: winning images are shown in two global exhibitions and included in the Life Framer photobook, alongside online exposure through the Life Framer site and channels. Life Framer also runs a separate Series Award for a solo exhibition and offers paid written feedback on submitted work; all prices are in US dollars. Animal Kingdom opens a new twelve-competition edition: the upcoming list marks a "NEW EDITION (AND EXHIBITIONS)" immediately before it. Note that the two surfaces print different years for the same round — the entry page gives "Deadline: 31 January 2027", while the competitions page's own card for Animal Kingdom still reads "31 January 2026", a date nine months past; the entry page is the one consistent with the rest of the sequence, and it lists the round as open for entries. The rules make the award "open to both amateur and professional photographers ... aged 18 years and over (or of the age of majority in jurisdictions in their respective country), and from all over the world", and bar employees, officers and agents of Life Framer or of anyone involved in running the award, along with their family relations. AI imagery is excluded outright: "We do not accept artificial intelligence or AI-generated imagery." Editing, post-processing, mixed media, collage and compositing are allowed provided photography is at the heart of the work, and there is no restriction on when an image was made. There is no rights grab — entrants keep full copyright, and Life Framer states it does not sell usage rights or use entries to train AI algorithms. Both the 1st and 2nd Prize photographers each month have their image exhibited in galleries around the world. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: $20–$100. Prize: $2,000.

item.title: Three Artist Exhibit · Decode Gallery
item.description: Decode Gallery in Tucson is looking for three photographers with a collective series of images — of any kind — to each take one of three spots in a three-person show. The three spots are different sizes: the gallery states the first hangs 6 images, the second 8 and the last 12. The call is for a body of work rather than single frames, and is open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional. Selection is by juror Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer who graduated with a BA in Photography from the Art Institute of Seattle in 2011 and whose work has been published internationally and exhibited nationally. The gallery handles all printing for the accepted photographers at no further cost, printing professionally on an Epson printer with Ilford Pearl paper, and makes one exhibition print per image, shown in museum-quality 22-inch white frames with precut mats; after the show each print is archived in a flat file for six months. Entry is $40 for up to fifteen photographs. Photographers are notified by email within two weeks of the deadline and high-resolution JPGs are due two days after the acceptance email. The exhibition runs 6 to 27 February 2027 at the gallery, opening 6 February. Work may be listed for sale, with Decode taking a 50 per cent commission; all rights to the image file and the print remain with the photographer. — Deadline: December 18, 2026. Fee: $40/15 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Open Call for Exhibition Proposals 2026 (3rd Edition) · Elliott Gallery
item.description: Elliott Gallery in Amsterdam runs its exhibition-proposal open call for the third year, with applications open from Monday 9 November to 30 November 2026. The medium is fine art photography exclusively — other artistic mediums are not considered — and there is no theme or subject restriction; the gallery is open to photographers worldwide, 18 and over, across all career stages, backgrounds and styles. Applicants submit one series of up to fifteen photographs as a link to a portfolio, cloud folder or file transfer, together with a statement of up to 200 words, through the gallery's Google Form. Three winning artists are selected. Each receives a six-week feature exhibition at the gallery, planned for March or April 2027 with exact dates agreed with the artists: two winners present alongside each other in the main exhibition room with around 20 m² of dedicated wall space each, and the third gets an intimate solo showcase in the separate back gallery, the Green Room, with around 10 m². All three also receive a curated digital exhibition on the gallery's website and channels, curatorial guidance, and a dedicated feature in the gallery's newsletters and social media, reaching its international network of collectors, curators and photography professionals. The terms set out what each side pays: the gallery hangs the show and covers labels, the exhibition catalogue, promotion and an opening reception, while the selected artists are responsible for the costs of producing, framing and shipping their own work. Sales during the exhibition are split 70 per cent to the artist and 30 per cent to the gallery, and a 12-month representation contract or another collaboration may be offered to winners or finalists. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed online before the final decision. The jury this edition is the British photographer Matthew Murray, winner of First Prize at the 2018 International Photography Awards for his Elliott Gallery monograph Saddleworth, and Leticia Valverdes, a photographer and TV producer who won the gallery's 2025 open call, with three of the gallery's own team. The non-refundable application fee is €35 per proposal, covers administration costs, and is charged once per submission. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: €35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2028 Artist Residency Grants · The Helene Wurlitzer Foundation of New Mexico
item.description: The Helene Wurlitzer Foundation, a private non-profit in Taos that has run one of the oldest artist residency programmes in the United States since 1954, is accepting applications for its 2028 residency grants. The grant is a 10- to 12-week stay — rent-free, utilities paid — in one of eleven fully furnished adobe casitas on the Foundation's Taos campus, and residents have no imposed expectations, quotas or requirements during their stay; the programme exists to give artists time and space. Photographers are named among the eligible visual arts disciplines alongside painters, sculptors, filmmakers and ceramicists, and the Foundation accepts applicants of national and international origin. Applications are scored blind: each is reviewed by a selection committee of professionals in the applicant's own discipline, and jurors know nothing about the artist's demographics, scoring in five categories purely on the merit of the work samples. Applicants submit five images, three references and a $30 application fee, online or by post. Two conditions attach to a grant rather than to applying: artists who are selected pay a $300 deposit, half of it retained for casita upkeep and half refundable against damage, and a no-work policy bars residents from being employed in Taos during the session. Applications submitted by 18 January 2027 at 11:59 PM Mountain Time are considered for three 2028 sessions — January to April and September to December, each twelve weeks, and June to August, ten weeks — with decisions notified by June 2027. — Deadline: January 18, 2027. Fee: $30. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Parallel Voices 2027 · Photometria International Photography Festival
item.description: Portfolio contest run by the Photometria International Photography Festival in Ioannina, Greece, open for submissions from 1 November to 15 December 2026. Entrants submit one portfolio of fifteen photographs, of which the jury selects eight; the subject is left to the photographer, with the festival asking for a coherent idea or a narrated story rather than a set theme. Nine portfolios are chosen and shown as a group exhibition titled "Parallel Voices" at the 2027 festival, its nineteenth edition, at a venue chosen by the organisers. Photometria covers production: the selected photographs are printed on canvas and installed at an outdoor venue, where the show runs about two months, and the prints are destroyed afterwards rather than returned. There is no cash prize or artist fee; selected photographers may take up discounted accommodation rates at properties the festival recommends, at their own cost. Selection criteria are the relevance of the pictures to the entrant's own topic, their coherence as a whole, and their artistic and aesthetic quality. The jury is the festival's own founders and artistic director. Entry is €20 per portfolio, paid through the festival's own photobookstore; the images go as 1500px JPGs by WeTransfer, SwissTransfer or FromSmash to the festival's portfolio address, together with a PDF carrying a bio, project description and artist statement. Results are announced by 15 February 2027. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: €20. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Darkroom Residencies 2027 · Spike Print Studio
item.description: Three six-week darkroom residencies at Spike Print Studio in Bristol for artists working in alternative photographic processes, running January to June 2027. Spike Print Studio is a charitable organisation and, in its own words, "the largest open-access print studio in the South West", printmaking in Bristol since 1976. This call is open only to artists based in the South West of England: the studio states it is "looking for three South West based artists who want to research, experiment and expand their current practice". Each residency gives up to four days of darkroom access a week (Mondays and Tuesdays guaranteed, Wednesdays and Thursdays bookable), a £200 materials budget, a place in a three-person exhibition at Spike Print Studio in June 2027 - timed to coincide with Spike Island's launch of British Art Show 10 - and a paid artist talk at Spike Island, hosted by Spike Print Studio, at which the three residents will appear in conversation together. Named areas of technical enquiry are cyanotype, gum bichromate, lith printing, phytogram, lumen printing, cliché verre and pinhole camera, and the studio is explicit that the list is not exhaustive. The darkroom holds a Durst M300 and a Durst C65 black-and-white enlarger (both 35mm), a printing frame, focus finder, test strip maker, contrast filters, a 1.2 x 1 m Natgraph metal-halide UV exposure unit, a table-top etching press with blankets and a 60 x 30 cm bed, an A2 lightbox, trays and tongs. Applicants must be able to work confidently and independently in their field, must come with a particular project or research enquiry to pursue over the six weeks, and must be willing to lead a small workshop for Spike Print Studio members. The three residency windows are 18 January to 4 March 2027 (no access in the week of 15 January), 8 March to 22 April 2027 (no access in the week of the 29th) and 26 April to 8 June 2027 (no access on 3 and 31 May), with the exhibition and artists' talk in June 2027, date to be confirmed. Applications opened on Thursday 5 November 2026 and close on Sunday 29 November 2026 at 23:59 GMT; shortlisted applicants are interviewed in the weeks of 30 November and 7 December 2026, and the selected artists are notified in the week of 14 December 2026. The application is a Google Form, and it asks for more than the call page lists: a 500-word statement on why you are applying and how the residency will benefit your practice, a 300-word description of your areas of expertise and the alternative photographic techniques you use, your preferred residency window, between three and five images of your work each under 1 MB, a referee's name, email and organisation, and your age. A CV may be attached but is optional, and a Google account is needed to upload the files. There is no application fee. — Deadline: November 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Six-week darkroom residency + £200 materials budget + three-person exhibition.

item.title: In Focus: A Juried Photography Exhibition · Art League of New Britain
item.description: Juried photography exhibition in the Art League of New Britain's Low Gallery, New Britain, Connecticut, 5 March - 18 April 2027, with an opening reception on Friday 5 March, 6-8 PM. The League presents it as "the return of a dedicated photography exhibition" to its historic gallery, and describes In Focus as examining "photography as both an artistic medium and a way of seeing" - bringing together work made through film, digital and experimental processes, and exploring the ways photographers use light, composition, perspective and subject matter to shape meaning. The brief is deliberately broad: documentary and portraiture, landscape, abstraction, conceptual work and experimental image-making are all named as welcome, and the organisers say the selected works should reflect "the diversity of contemporary photographic practice and the individual viewpoints that define it". Eligibility is explicit that "works must be photographs" - this is not a mixed-media show with a photography slot. The juror is Florin Ion Firimită, a Romanian-born visual artist, photographer and writer who was introduced to photography as a child through his father's darkroom and later fled communist Romania; his work has appeared in more than 400 exhibitions across four continents, including Paris, Milan, Venice and New York, is held in collections including the Rodin Museum in Paris, and his photographic series The Library has had international recognition. Jurying is hybrid and anonymous: work is selected online from unsigned photographs, then prize winners are chosen in person after drop-off, so the physical print decides the awards. Awards total $400 - $200 first prize, $100 second, $50 third, plus a $25 Honorable Mention and a $25 Juror's Pick. Each artist may enter up to five works, completed in the past three years, original and not previously exhibited in any ALNB show; framed work may not exceed 42 inches in width or height. Entry is $25 for a first work and $15 for each subsequent work, or $15 and $10 for ALNB members, and fees are non-refundable. Registration runs 5 November 2026 to 21 January 2027, with the submission deadline at 11:59 PM on 21 January and notifications on Saturday 30 January 2027. 2D work must arrive ready to hang with wire, D-rings or screw eyes - no sawtooth hangers and no easel-back frames, with prints on metal with a keyhole hanger the exception - and image files must be JPEGs under 4 MB in sRGB, ideally at least 1920 pixels on the longest side. AI-generated imagery is not acceptable; AI-assisted work must be clearly disclosed at submission and must include meaningful creative input, editing or direction by the artist, and failure to disclose may mean disqualification from awards or prizes. Open to all artists aged 18 and over. — Deadline: January 21, 2027. Fee: $25 first entry, $15 after (members $15/$10). Prize: $400 total: $200 / $100 / $50 + $25 Honorable Mention + $25 Juror's Pick + exhibition.

item.title: SAGE Magazine 2027 Print Edition — Marginalia (in nature)
item.description: SAGE Magazine is a student-run environmental publication of the Yale School of the Environment in New Haven, Connecticut, in print since 2006. What began as a small internal publication for environmental graduate students has become, in the magazine's own words, a sought-after publication for poets, writers, visual artists, comic book creators, graphic designers and environmentalists expressing themselves through art; its stated goal is expanding environmentalism through provocative conversation and the arts. The digital magazine publishes year-round and an Annual Print Issue appears each spring, alongside events, speakers and workshops on environmental writing, journalism and the arts. Submissions are now open for the 2027 print edition on the theme Marginalia (in nature). Marginalia as traditionally defined refers to notes, comments or artwork written or drawn in the margins of a book or manuscript, and in these margins, the editors write, "we emphasize, interpret, argue, daydream"; the issue asks what is written, argued, archived and dreamed in the margins of environments, landscapes and ecosystems big and small, inviting photographers and artists to "take us to these edges and peripheries". SAGE seeks provocative, critical, beautiful, captivating work from emerging and established environmental writers and artists, welcomes pieces ranging from playful to pensive, and describes its throughline as strengthening and exploring the relationship between humanity and the environment. Four categories are accepted: prose (personal essays, narrative journalism and short stories up to 3,000 words), poetry, photography and photo essays, and visual art. Contributors may submit up to three pieces. Work must be previously unpublished; simultaneous submissions are welcome, but a submission must be withdrawn if it is accepted elsewhere. Rolling gallery submissions are no longer accepted. There is no entry fee, and submission is through the magazine's own Google Form. The deadline is 14 December 2026. The editors note that response times vary because the publication is student-run, and ask that contributors not email about the status of a submission. The current masthead is Editor-in-Chief Sara Sherburne and Managing Editor Olivia Bayne. The submission form carries three requirements the call page does not: each piece needs its own form submission, only one file may be uploaded per form (PDF, document, drawing or image, maximum 10 MB), and visual work should be a .png, .raw or high-quality .jpeg of at least 300 dpi. The form's Type of Submission list offers only visual art, poetry and prose, so a photograph is entered as visual art, and its required affiliation question reads "university or independent", so no Yale connection is needed. Contributors receive no confirmation email. One thing to read past: the same page also advertises a compensated designer position for the 2027 print edition with a 13 November 2026 deadline, applied for through Yale Student Employment - that is a job posting, not part of this call for work. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Trois Points Mag Vol 16 — The Future
item.description: Trois Points Mag is an independent contemporary photography magazine made by an international team of artists based in Paris. It was founded in 2016 as an online-only publication, paused through the covid years and came back in December 2022 both online and as a high-quality printed issue; its stated concept is to promote new contemporary photography, analog and digital, from photographers anywhere in the world, always around a proposed theme. Vol 16, the Winter 2026 paper issue, is themed The Future, and the magazine's question is "What does the future look like before it happens?" The editors are interested in visions of what is yet to come - imagined, anticipated, feared, desired or remembered - and say the future may be technological or primitive, intimate or collective, utopian or dystopian, real or impossible, emerging through landscapes, bodies, architecture, objects, rituals, altered realities or everyday moments: "There is no single future. Show us yours." Submissions go by email with the subject line "Vol 16 / The Future": up to 15 images per project, each file titled with the photographer's full name, at 300 dpi in a large file format and under 50 MB in total. A short text of three or four sentences about the theme is mandatory and is what gets printed alongside the work if selected - the magazine explicitly does not want a general artist statement - together with a brief four-or-five-sentence bio rather than a CV, website and social links, and the photographer's current city and country. The camera used must be named, and captures made with an iPhone or other smartphone are not accepted. There is no entry fee; the magazine suggests a voluntary 5 euro donation to help sustain the project. The deadline is 30 November 2026. CAUTION: the magazine's own website has not been updated for this issue — www.troispointsmag.com/submissions still presents Vol 11 (Autumn 2025, "The Consuming World") as its newest call, with a 12-image cap, so the brief above is the one the magazine published on its own Instagram on 5 October 2026 and the website's guidelines page does not match it. The magazine's standing terms add that every image must be the artist's own original work, that files are accepted in digital format only, that there is no payment for publication — a contributor buys a copy of the magazine only if they want one — and that submitting grants permission to publish the image together with the photographer's name and city of residence. SECOND CAUTION, MEASURED 10 NOVEMBER 2026 AND THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE PASS TO FAIL: that Instagram post no longer serves its caption, so none of the terms above can be re-confirmed at source. The post page still loads with its like count and its 5 October 2026 date, but the caption element renders empty and Instagram’s own embed endpoint for the same post answers “The link to this photo or video may be broken, or the post may have been removed”. Captions on the magazine’s other posts do still read and the account is active — it posted on 9 November — so nothing says the call has closed; but the deadline, the voluntary donation and the fifteen-image cap all rest on one reading of a caption that is now unreadable. Confirm with the magazine before sending work. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free (voluntary €5 donation). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Paper Route: Contemporary Works on Paper · Arts Benicia
item.description: Arts Benicia, the nonprofit visual arts centre that has run exhibitions and classes in Benicia, California for more than 39 years, is jurying Paper Route: Contemporary Works on Paper for its gallery in the Commanding Officer's Quarters. The call treats paper not as a support but as a collaborator: the organiser's own text describes work "from the fluid immediacy of watercolor and the stark precision of ink, to the layered textures of mixed media and printmaking", unified by a single material constraint that "reveal[s] how the unique tooth, fiber, and weight of the paper substrate dictate the behavior of different mediums". All 2D and 3D media are accepted, work may be of any subject or abstract, and photographers are specifically provided for: the entry terms bar giclée prints "except for photos", so an inkjet photographic print is eligible where an inkjet reproduction of a painting is not. Two-dimensional work may not exceed 36 inches wide or 72 inches high including the frame, 3D work is capped at a 36 by 36 inch footprint, hanging work is limited to 35 pounds, wall works must be wired and sawtooth hangers are not accepted. Work previously shown at Arts Benicia is not eligible. One application covers up to six artworks. Entry is $45 for the first work, or $35 for current Arts Benicia members, plus $5 for each additional work up to six - five works cost a non-member $65. The member rate is checked: "Only use the member entry price if you are a current member, otherwise your entry will not be juried." National and international artists are invited to apply. Entries close 12 January 2027 at 11:59pm Pacific, jurying runs 14-24 January and artists are notified on 27 January 2027. The juror is Margot Yale, assistant curator of prints and drawings at the Achenbach Foundation for Graphic Arts, who joined the Achenbach from the Metropolitan Museum of Art, where she was an Andrew W. Mellon Fellow in Modern and Contemporary Art. Hand delivery and shipped work are both due by 11 March 2027, with an artists' preview on Thursday 1 April, 6-7pm and a public opening reception on Saturday 3 April, 4-6pm; the exhibition runs 3 April to 16 May 2027 and work is picked up on 18 May. Work must be available for sale and Arts Benicia retains 40% of any sale, paying the artist 60% within 30 days of closing. Artists who ship must include a prepaid return label. There is no cash award: selection into the gallery exhibition is the outcome. — Deadline: January 12, 2027. Fee: $45 ($35 members) + $5/additional entry. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 17th Annual Intercollegiate Student Art Competition · Center for Contemporary Arts
item.description: The Center for Contemporary Arts in downtown Abilene, Texas runs its Intercollegiate Student Art Competition for a seventeenth year, and photography is one of its four judged categories alongside non-digital 2D, digitally created 2D and 3D work. Entry is free and open to students enrolled at Abilene-area and regional colleges and universities; each student may submit up to two pieces in any medium that meets the category's size and weight limits, and work must be original and not previously exhibited at the CCA. Entries are juried by professional contemporary artists, and selected work hangs in Gallery 3 at the CCA from 4 December 2026 to 23 January 2027, with a closing reception and awards on 23 January, 5-7pm. Cash prizes are $300 for Best in Show and $100 for First Place in each of the four categories, including First Place Photography; those five winners also receive a one-year CCA Student Artist Membership, with the usual 20-hour volunteer requirement and application fee waived for a year. Photographs and digital prints must be matted and at least 8 by 10 inches, framed unless canvas-wrapped or mounted on board with proper hanging equipment, no wider than 48 inches, no taller than 60 inches and under 30 pounds. Submission is through the organiser's online entry form, one form per piece, and work must be delivered in person to 220 Cypress Street in Abilene on 28 November, 11am-5pm, or by noon on Monday 30 November; late entries are not accepted even when the form arrived on time. Unselected work is collected after notification, exhibited work from 25 to 30 January 2027, and the prospectus warns that anything left more than 30 days past those dates becomes CCA property. Awards are Best in Show and Best in Category, with optional second, third and honourable mentions. — Deadline: November 28, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $300 Best in Show + $100 First Place Photography + exhibition.

item.title: Artsin Square Prize 2026
item.description: First edition of the Artsin Square Prize, an international open call run by Artsin Square, the independent artist-run publisher behind the magazine, artist books and the 5×7 photobook series. One artist receives a $1,000 cash prize, a feature in the print edition of Artsin Square magazine, an interview published on the Artsin Square website and a permanent artist feature there, plus promotion through the newsletter and social channels; up to three shortlisted artists get a dedicated online presentation and social promotion, and the organiser states that no further fee is asked of the winner or the shortlisted artists. There is no set theme, so applicants submit work that best represents their current practice, and any visual medium is eligible — photography is named alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, textile, installation, collage, digital art and mixed media. Artists at all career stages may apply, collectives count as one applicant, and galleries or arts organisations may submit on an artist's behalf with permission. Submit 3 to 10 works as JPEGs no larger than 5 MB, uploaded through the application form; an artist biography of up to 250 words is optional. The entry form sells three fixed bundles — 3 images at $30, 5 at $35 and 10 at $40 — and its upload field asks applicants to choose 3, 5 or 10 images and upload the same number, so the stated 3-to-10 range is bought in those three steps. Applications are reviewed by the Artsin Square selection committee on artistic and conceptual strength, originality, quality and consistency of the work and the development of the artist's practice, with the committee's decision final. Finalists and the winner are announced in the first week of December 2026 and all applicants are told the result by email. Entry grants Artsin Square permission to use the submitted images in connection with the prize — in the print magazine, on the website, in interviews and through the newsletter and social media — if the artist is selected as winner or shortlisted. — Deadline: November 25, 2026. Fee: $30 for 3 images, $35 for 5, $40 for 10. Prize: $1,000 cash + publication in Artsin Square magazine.

item.title: The Art of Street Photography · TCG Gallery
item.description: TCG Gallery invites photographers and lens-based artists worldwide to submit work for The Art of Street Photography, an online exhibition of photographs made in public life. The gallery's framing is that the street offers no arrangement and no second take — a gesture, a collision of shapes, a person passing through a patch of light — and that what matters is what the photographer sees in the moment. Photographs from cities, small towns, neighbourhoods, transit spaces and other places where public life unfolds are welcome, and the prospectus states explicitly that people need not appear in every frame. Digital, film, alternative-process and mixed-media photographic work is accepted. Work is reviewed for visual strength, originality, photographic execution, relevance to the theme and contribution to a coherent exhibition. Images generated by, or substantially altered with, generative AI are not eligible. Each entry takes up to three photographs — one is enough, the other two slots are optional — as JPG or JPEG files at least 1,200 pixels on the longest side, unwatermarked and unsigned, with a descriptive filename; multiple entries are permitted and the $15 fee is charged per entry, with fee waivers available through the gallery's waiver application. Entrants supply name, email and location plus title, year, medium, physical print dimensions and price or NFS for each work; website, Instagram, biography and image descriptions are optional. Selected photographs appear in a curated online exhibition running 1–31 January 2027 with artist and artwork information, remain in the gallery's long-term exhibition archive, and may be promoted by email and through the gallery's social channels. Work may be offered for sale or marked not for sale, and TCG Gallery retains a 30% commission on anything sold through it. Copyright remains with the artist; selected artists grant nonexclusive permission for credited exhibition, archiving and related gallery promotion. The cutoff has a time: the call is headed "DEADLINE DECEMBER 20, 2026, 11:59 PM ET" and repeats "Submission deadline: December 20, 2026, 11:59 PM ET", with artist notifications on 27 December 2026. — Deadline: December 20, 2026. Fee: $15 per entry (up to 3 images); fee waivers available. Prize: Online exhibition.
